current_description.description_long: On February 17, 1999, the Washington Post reported that Evercore Partners had agreed to acquire American Media Inc., the Florida-based publisher of the National Enquirer and Star. The reported transaction included Evercore assuming American Media’s debt. David Pecker, then chief executive of Hachette Filipacchi Magazines, was hired to become American Media’s chairman and chief executive. The distinction between buying the publisher and taking its top job matters: the transaction was led by Evercore, while Pecker became the executive responsible for running the company. The record’s earlier title incorrectly described Pecker as personally buying the National Enquirer and called the publication Mafia-owned. The cited 1999 acquisition report does not support either assertion. It also does not establish a Trump-related purpose or connection in the transaction itself. Pecker’s later relationship with Donald Trump should not be projected backward onto this corporate change. The revised description is limited to the ownership transaction and Pecker’s appointment, both reported at the time. Separate evidence would be required for the publication’s earlier financing history or for any later political relationship involving its leadership.

frozen_original.title: Trump Calls Fauci 'Dr. Death' and Claims He Funded COVID Creation (2023)
frozen_original.synopsis: Following Dr. Anthony Fauci's retirement from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in December 2022, Donald Trump intensified attacks on the nation's most prominent infectious disease expert, calling him 'Dr. Death' and repeatedly claiming Fauci had funded the creation of COVID-19 through gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. Trump called for Fauci to be prosecuted and jailed. While legitimate scientific debate exists about specific NIH funding grants to EcoHealth Alliance, the claim that Fauci personally funded COVID's creation as a bioweapon was unsupported by intelligence or scientific evidence. Congress investigated the NIH grants and found no evidence of deliberate pathogen creation. Trump's attacks on Fauci generated death threats against the scientist and his family, requiring permanent security protection.

frozen_original.title: Trump Administration Gives $1.5 Billion Tax Cuts to Private Equity in CARES Act
frozen_original.synopsis: Hidden within the $2.2 trillion CARES Act pandemic relief legislation signed on March 27, 2020, were provisions providing an estimated $1.5 billion in tax benefits specifically for private equity firms and wealthy investors. The episode exemplified how Trump's pandemic response legislation served wealthy donors alongside ordinary relief.
